1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Larchmere Care Group runs nine residential care homes. Two homes in the town of Calderbridge, Ashby Fold (52 beds, two floors) and Penmor Lodge (44 beds, two floors), have piloted a reduced night-staffing rota since 1 June 2026. Group rollout of the rota to the other seven homes is planned for March 2027. You are the group quality lead, writing in mid-October 2026.
9	Your request: The Director of Operations wants a recommendation for the 12 November 2026 board. Should the group put Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge back on four night staff and halt the March 2027 rollout of the pilot rota? What explains the rise in recorded falls at the two homes?
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Email from Marian Telfer, Director of Operations, to the group quality lead, 6 October 2026 (leadership-account): Subject: Calderbridge falls - board recommendation. Falls at our two night-rota pilot homes have nearly doubled: 16 in Q2, 31 in Q3 (Ashby Fold 9 to 17, Penmor Lodge 7 to 14). Since 1 June both homes have run nights with three staff (one carer per floor plus a floating senior) instead of four (two carers per floor). That is the obvious change. Night staff tell me they can't get to call bells as fast. We have no call-bell timings from before June, but I believe them. I want a recommendation for the 12 November board: put both homes back on four night staff now and pull the March rollout to the other seven homes. I am not prepared to wait another quarter.
12	- Group quality dashboard extract, Q3 2026, falls section (system-record): Recorded falls, Q2 to Q3 2026: Ashby Fold 9 to 17 (RED); Penmor Lodge 7 to 14 (RED); Brackenhill 11 to 9; Cresswell Court 8 to 9; Dunmore House 14 to 12; Elmstead 6 to 7; Fairholme 10 to 11; Greywater 12 to 9; Hatherley View 7 to 8. Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge combined, by month: Apr 4, May 5, Jun 7, Jul 11, Aug 9, Sep 11. RAG rule: red where the quarter-on-quarter rise exceeds 25%. Notes: figures are raw counts, not adjusted for occupancy. From 1 July, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge incidents are imported directly from the Tallyline incident app. All other homes' figures are keyed in from paper incident forms by site administrators.
13	- Interview notes, night senior carers at Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge, 2-3 October 2026 (taken by the deputy quality lead) (staff-account): Ashby Fold night senior (9 years in post): 'With one carer per floor, if two bells go at once on the same floor somebody waits. We're slower, I'm sure of it, though I couldn't give you minutes.' Penmor Lodge night senior (in the floating role since June): 'It's different, not worse. Because I float, I'm usually free for the second bell. A lot of what's on the system now is people found sitting on the floor at the two o'clock check with no injury. We always had those. Whether they all got written up before, I honestly couldn't say.'
14	- Incident system query: falls by time of day, Ashby Fold and Penmor Lodge combined, Q2 and Q3 2026 (system-record): Night (22:00-07:00): Q2 8, Q3 18. Day (07:00-22:00): Q2 8, Q3 13. Night share of falls: Q2 50%, Q3 58%. Day staffing at both homes did not change during either quarter. Source note: Q2 times come from paper forms. The time field was blank on 3 forms, and the administrator assigned those from the shift recorded. Q3 times are stamped automatically by Tallyline when the entry is made, which may be some time after the fall was discovered.
15	- Replies from the two registered managers to the Director of Operations, 7 October 2026 (manager-account): Penmor Lodge manager: 'I don't think it's the rota. Since Hollin Street Medical Practice took over our residents in May, the new GPs have been reviewing everyone's medication, and some residents have been started on night-time tablets. I'd look there first.' Ashby Fold manager: 'We moved to Hollin Street in May as well. My worry is admissions. We've taken more people from the hospital discharge-to-assess beds this summer, and they arrive frailer than our usual referrals. The rota is tight, but I'm not convinced it's the whole story.'
16	
17	BRIEF:
18	I can't yet say that the new night rota caused the rise in falls, and I would not recommend reversing it or halting the rollout now.
19	
20	What the evidence shows: the rise coincides with the switch to the incident app on 1 July. Q2 was an unusually low quarter at both homes, near the bottom of their history. Handover notes show some Q2 falls were never written up. The growth is concentrated in no-harm and "found on floor" events, while serious falls (GP or hospital attendance) barely moved, from 2 to 3. Q3 rates sit inside the homes' long-run limits. Other homes have had similar jumps that reversed.
21	
22	What I can't rule out: a real rota effect, frailer admissions, or medication changes. A sustained 40% rise would take 2–3 quarters to show on the chart. We have no pre-June call-bell data. Ashby Fold answers a median of 3m40s, but there is nothing to compare it with. Penmor Lodge's call system can't record answer times at all.
23	
24	Next steps: keep the pilot running under its pause criteria. Show falls as rates on the control chart, with the reporting change marked. Start manual sampling of night call-bell response times now. Track admissions' frailty and medication changes. Decide on the rollout at a dated review in late January using Q4 data. Don't discipline staff, and don't withdraw the app.
25
